Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Angola enacted Law 22/11 on the Protection of Personal Data on 17 June 2011, making it one of 36 African countries with a Data Protection Act. The law establishes data processing principles (transparency, lawfulness, proportionality, purpose, accuracy), regulates sensitive data (including biometric/genetic data), and requires notification/authorisation by the Data Protection Agency (APD). Angola also ratified the Malabo Convention. A draft amendment to the DPA is in progress to address AI and digital ID.
revision_notes: Fetched and confirmed both cited sources. Hunton Andrews Kurth (2011) and the CMS Expert Guide (updated October 2025) confirm Law 22/11 of 17 June 2011 on the Protection of Personal Data remains in force, covering biometric and other sensitive data and establishing the Data Protection Agency (APD). No subsequent Act has replaced it (a draft AI/digital-ID amendment is reportedly in progress but not yet enacted). Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Angola has enacted comprehensive data protection legislation. Law 22/11 of 17 June 2011 on the Protection of Personal Data establishes data processing principles (transparency, lawfulness, proportionality, purpose limitation, accuracy), regulates sensitive data including biometric and genetic data, and requires notification to, or authorisation from, the Data Protection Agency (Agência de Protecção de Dados, APD) for data processing activities linked to the ID system.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Angolan Data Protection Agency (Agência de Proteção de Dados, APD) was formally constituted in 2016 (some sources cite October 2019 as when it became operational) under Law 22/11 to oversee collection and processing of personal data, enforce data protection legislation and apply sanctions. The APD has intensified supervisory activities in recent years and has levied significant financial fines against non-compliant organisations. It is responsible for approving international data transfers and authorising processing of sensitive data.
revision_notes: PLMJ legal update (August 2024) confirms the Agência de Protecção de Dados (APD), formally constituted in 2016 under Law 22/11, has intensified enforcement, issuing fines of USD 75,000-150,000 against several companies in 2024 (e.g. MAXAM, Banco Comercial do Huambo) for data protection breaches including unauthorised international transfers and failure to notify processing activities. This is more recent and specific evidence of active oversight than the original 2019 'became operational' date. Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed; year updated to the latest documented enforcement activity.
revised_comments: Angola's Data Protection Agency (Agência de Protecção de Dados, APD), established under Law 22/11 and formally constituted in 2016, actively regulates the collection, processing and sharing of personal data, including data linked to the ID system. The APD has intensified its supervisory role, issuing financial sanctions of USD 75,000 to USD 150,000 against several companies in 2024 for breaches such as unauthorised international data transfers and failure to notify data processing activities. It is also responsible for approving international data transfers and authorising the processing of sensitive data.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Under Law 4/09 as originally enacted, national IDs were mandated from age 10. Law 3/21 (2021 amendment) removed the minimum age requirement, making the ID available to all ages including newborns. A November 2025 initiative began issuing ID cards to newborns in Zaire Province. Law 4/09 specifies the first issuance is free for applicants aged 6-11. The enrollment eligibility of 6-10 years (category 3) is supported; with the 2021 amendment opening it to younger ages.
revision_notes: Read the actual legal text of Law 3/21 of 25 January 2021 (lex.ao), which amends Law 4/09 and states enrolment applies 'sem qualquer limitação de idade' (without any age limitation) - i.e. from birth, nationwide. This has since been operationalised: Biometric Update (17 Nov 2025) confirms Angola began issuing ID cards to newborns via the 'Born with a Birth Certificate' campaign with UNICEF, piloted in Zaire Province and expanding to other municipalities. The original score of 3 (6-10 years) reflected only the age bracket for free first issuance under Law 4/09, not the actual minimum eligibility age, which has been under 1 year since the 2021 amendment. Recalculated to 5 (<1).
revised_comments: Angola's national ID (Bilhete de Identidade) is legally available from birth. Law 3/21 of 25 January 2021, amending Law 4/09 on the Civil Identification Regime, removed the previous minimum age requirement and applies to identification and issuance of the Bilhete de Identidade Nacional 'without any age limitation'. This has since been operationalised, with authorities beginning to issue ID cards to newborns from November 2025 under the 'Born with a Birth Certificate' campaign, launched with UNICEF support, starting in Zaire Province and expanding to further municipalities.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: According to the UN Centre of Excellence for CRVS and the World Bank ID4D Diagnostic (2024), in 2022 approximately 46% of Angolan citizens had an ID card (BI). The Paradigm Initiative policy brief (2024) notes 14 million out of 33 million Angolans (approximately 42%) hold an identity card. The World Bank 2017 data cited 28% biometric national ID coverage. Birth registration stands at 77% (2022 UN data). The 46% BI coverage places Angola in the 20-49% range.
revision_notes: Updated with the most recent available figure: Angola's Minister of Justice and Human Rights stated (Angola Press Agency, reported via allAfrica, 1-2 July 2026) that the national ID (BI) database registers nearly 16 million citizens, of whom approximately 14 million are adults, against a total population of roughly 37 million - approximately 43%. This is consistent with the previously cited 2022 World Bank/UN CRVS figure of approximately 46% and confirms the 20-49% band (code 2). Score confirmed unchanged; year updated to reflect the newest available figure.
revised_comments: Approximately 43-46% of Angola's population holds a national ID card (Bilhete de Identidade). As of mid-2026, the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights reported that almost 16 million citizens (around 14 million adults) are registered in the national ID database, against a total population of roughly 37 million. This aligns with the 2022 World Bank/UN Centre of Excellence for CRVS estimate of approximately 46% BI coverage, placing Angola within the 20-49% coverage band. Birth registration coverage is higher, at around 77% (2022).
